items.title: Equivalent fractions and comparison
items.content: Multiply or divide numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number. Compare unlike fractions using a common denominator or cross-products.

items.title: Four operations
items.content: Add/subtract with a common denominator. Multiply numerators and denominators. Divide by multiplying by the reciprocal of the nonzero divisor. Simplify the result.

items.title: Exam checks
items.content:
Estimate the size before calculating to catch an implausible result.
Cancel common factors before multiplying to keep numbers small.

items.title: Proper, improper and mixed fractions
items.content: A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator; an improper fraction has numerator at least as large. Worked example: \(17/5=3\frac25\); \(3\frac25=17/5\).

items.title: Simplifying and equivalence
items.content: Divide top and bottom by a common factor. Worked example: \(42/56=3/4\), dividing each by 14.

items.title: Compare unlike denominators
items.content: Worked example: compare \(5/8\) and \(2/3\). Cross-products are 15 and 16, so \(5/8<2/3\).

items.title: Addition and subtraction
items.content: Worked example: \(2/3+3/8=16/24+9/24=25/24=1\frac1{24}\). Use the least common denominator when practical.

items.title: Multiplication and cancellation
items.content: Worked example: \(6/15\times25/18\). Cancel across: \(6/18=1/3\), \(25/15=5/3\), so result \(5/9\).

items.title: Division and reciprocal
items.content: Worked example: \(3/4\div2/5=3/4\times5/2=15/8=1\frac78\).

items.title: Fraction of a quantity and word problems
items.content: Worked example: \(3/5\) of 40 is \(40\times3/5=24\). “Of” indicates multiplication.

items.title: Multiply fractions or mixed numbers
items.content: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions, cancel, then multiply. Worked example: \(1\frac12\times2\frac23=3/2\times8/3=4\).

items.title: Divide by a fraction
items.content: Worked example: \(5/6\div10/9=5/6\times9/10=3/4\).

items.title: Find a fraction of an amount
items.content: Worked example: \(7/8\) of ₹640 is \(640/8\times7=₹560\).

items.title: Find the whole from a fractional part
items.content: Worked example: \(3/7\) of a class is 12 students. Whole class is \(12\times7/3=28\).

items.title: Compare or order fractions
items.content: Use common denominators or cross multiplication; account for negative signs separately. Worked example: 5/8 < 2/3 because 5·3 = 15 < 16 = 2·8.

items.title: Why equivalent fractions keep value
items.content: Multiplying by \(k/k=1\), for nonzero \(k\), gives \(a/b=ak/bk\). The ratio is unchanged.

items.title: Why a common denominator is needed for addition
items.content: Fractions count equal-sized parts. Convert to the same part size before combining: \(a/b+c/d=(ad+bc)/bd\), for nonzero denominators.

items.title: Why division uses a reciprocal
items.content: To divide \(a/b\) by \(c/d\), find the number that multiplied by \(c/d\) gives \(a/b\). Multiplying by \(d/c\) cancels \(c/d\); the divisor must be nonzero.

sections.title: Common errors and how to avoid them

items.title: Adding denominators
items.content: Do not add denominators. First rewrite both fractions with the same denominator.

items.title: Reciprocating the wrong fraction
items.content: For division, keep the first fraction and invert only the divisor.

items.title: Incorrect whole-number conversion
items.content: For \(a\frac bc\), use \((ac+b)/c\), retaining the denominator.

items.title: Not simplifying or stating units
items.content: Reduce when possible and include the unit for quantity problems.

keyTakeaways: Equivalent fractions multiply numerator and denominator by the same factor.
Division by a fraction means multiplication by its reciprocal.
